frontier.hypothesis: F26 — the residual is entirely inside sched.c's ready-list ordering, and the candidate's win (both `lbu` at the block head) and the const chassis's win (`sw 16(sp)` before `lw a3`) are separated by ONE tie-break decision that no C-level spelling has moved in 65 forms.
frontier.mechanism: With expand order settled from calls.c and the alias class ruled out, the block's order depends only on INSN_PRIORITY (fixed by the arithmetic) and rank_for_schedule's tie-breaks (load/store class against last_scheduled_insn, then INSN_LUID). The candidate and the const chassis differ in exactly one bit — RTX_UNCHANGING_P on one load — and that bit flips both the `lbu` order and the arg3 chain's position, the signature of a tie-break cascade rather than a dependence change.
frontier.next_probe: Run the instrumented cc1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1, BB2_PRIO_DEBUG / BB2_SCHED_DEBUG — see the instrumented-cc1-location memory) on the candidate AND on the const chassis using tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s10/idump.sh + schedscan.py, and diff the two RANKDBG traces over build idx 46-61. A two-form diff of one chassis differing in one bit isolates the exact comparison that flips: if it is an INSN_LUID tie the lever is a source-order change to the two index reads on the const chassis; if it is the load/store class test the lever is which insn precedes the pair.
